teams.heading: Fiji drop to 12th in standings after suffering defeat against Scotland
teams.body: In their last five games, Fiji have won one match. They have lost four of those five matches. Their most recent fixture ended in a 20-15 home defeat against Japan in September 2026 during the knockout stage of the Pacific Nations Cup. In the current tournament, the team sit 12th in the standings after three matches. The side has suffered three losses from those three games, most recently falling 17-33 to Scotland.

teams.heading: Premiership agrees refereeing revamp to boost Steve Borthwick's World Cup plans
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has secured a significant structural boost ahead of next year's World Cup in Australia. Premiership Rugby has agreed to a refereeing revamp for the upcoming domestic season to better align club officiating with the international game. Following a meeting between Borthwick and directors of rugby, the RFU's refereeing team will adjust interpretations around the offside line, the scrum's brake-foot law, and the breakdown, targeting areas of previous inconsistency.

lead.why: The Premiership's refereeing overhaul directly aligns club officiating with the international game, handing Steve Borthwick a major World Cup preparation boost.

teams.heading: French Rugby Federation faces scrutiny over secret player workload management agreement
teams.body: Debate continues to swirl around the disclosure of a secret agreement between the FFR and LNR regarding the management of 33 elite players. While intended to regulate playing time ahead of next year's World Cup, the late revelation of the list has caused consternation among fans and clubs alike. Concerns persist regarding how this rotation policy, which mandates specific rest periods and limits to annual Test appearances, will influence team selections during the upcoming Six Nations tournament.

teams.heading: Ireland U20 Star Noah Byrne Departs Leinster For Australian Rules Move
teams.body: Emerging full-back Noah Byrne has opted to leave Irish rugby, rejecting a professional academy contract with Leinster to pursue a career with the Brisbane Lions in the AFL. The 20-year-old, who started every match for Ireland during this year’s Under-20 Six Nations campaign, was considered one of the most promising back-three prospects in the country. Leinster academy manager Peter Smyth confirmed the move, noting that while the decision is a blow, the province’s door remains open to the talented dual-athlete.

teams.heading: Italy Men’s Team Prepare To Face South Africa In Turin Stadium
teams.body: Top-level international rugby returns to the Allianz Stadium this November as Italy prepare to host reigning world champions South Africa. This match serves as the Azzurri's first home fixture in the newly established Nations Championship. The event was officially presented at the stadium on Sunday, 20 September, highlighting the venue's role as a recurring host for high-profile tests. Gonzalo Quesada’s side will look to build on this momentum, having already contested away matches in Japan, New Zealand and Australia.

lead.why: The return of top-level international rugby to Turin for the upcoming Nations Championship fixture is the key development in the men's senior schedule.

teams.heading: Scotland winger Darcy Graham ruled out of upcoming November international series
teams.body: Scotland and Edinburgh winger Darcy Graham will miss the upcoming Nations Championship matches against New Zealand, Australia, and Japan after suffering a ruptured bicep. Edinburgh head coach Sean Everitt confirmed the injury, sustained in a recent friendly, will sideline the 29-year-old for at least 12 weeks. Everitt noted the disappointment of the news, stating, "That's not good news for us and not good news for him, especially with the autumn series coming up." Graham is currently Scotland's leading try-scorer.

lead.why: The news of Darcy Graham's long-term injury significantly impacts Scotland's upcoming autumn international squad.

teams.heading: Wales Women's Seren Lockwood ruled out for upcoming USA Test fixture
teams.body: Scrum-half Seren Lockwood has been ruled out of the Wales Women's second WXV Global Series match against the USA this Saturday. Lockwood sustained a head injury during the first half of the side's victory over South Africa and is currently following World Rugby’s return-to-play protocols. Head coach Sean Lynn confirmed that while her absence is a loss, it provides an opportunity for Lleucu George to return at fly-half, with Keira Bevan shifting to her usual position at nine.

teams.heading: The Pumas hammer the Iberians in commanding Tbilisi display
teams.body: The Pumas recorded an emphatic 64-21 victory over Spain's Iberians in Tbilisi after leading 40-14 at half-time. Left wing Tino Swanepoel delivered a standout performance by crossing five times as the side ran in 10 tries during the fixture. Clinton Swart added a try alongside five conversions, while further tries came from Wian van Niekerk, Gustav du Rand, Alfondso Isaacs and André Fouché to seal the win.

lead.why: The Pumas dominated the Iberians with a 10-try haul in Tbilisi.

teams.heading: Les Kiss shifts Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to wing for Springboks Test
teams.body: Wallabies coach Les Kiss is set to move outside centre Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to the wing for Sunday's Test against the Springboks in Perth. The switch would mark the first time since the 23-year-old crossed to rugby union that he starts a Test anywhere other than outside centre, with Hunter Paisami expected to start at inside centre and Len Ikitau returning to No 13. Kiss's decision is understood to leverage Suaalii's aerial ability against South Africa's contested kicking game, adding height to the Wallabies' back three.

teams.heading: Japan Brave Blossoms Win Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup 2026
teams.body: The Brave Blossoms secured their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 by defeating holders Fiji 20-15 in a fiercely physical Test match at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. Captain Naoto Saito described the victory as a great breakthrough to create history for a young team entering the World Rugby top 10 rankings. Mamoru Harada and Ben Gunter scored tries to overturn a half-time deficit in a hard-fought contest.

teams.heading: Scott Barrett set for long-awaited return via Taranaki NPC clash
teams.body: Former New Zealand captain Scott Barrett is back to full fitness and will make his long-awaited return to action this weekend in a National Provincial Championship match for Taranaki against Hawke's Bay. Sidelined for the entire season with a bulging disc that required surgery, Barrett admitted the injury depowered his left side and prevented him from running. The 32-year-old lock, who last played for the team against Wales at the end of 2025, will pack down in the second-row alongside fellow All Black Josh Lord at McLean Park.

lead.why: Scott Barrett is returning from a long-term back injury to play for Taranaki this weekend.

teams.heading: Andre Esterhuizen captains changed men's team for Australia Test
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has named Andre Esterhuizen as captain of a heavily rotated Springboks men's side for Sunday's clash against the Wallabies in Perth. The head coach has made 13 changes to his starting XV following the victory over New Zealand, retaining only Eben Etzebeth and Ethan Hooker from the run-on team. Erasmus praised the new skipper by saying, “He captained the Hollywoodbets Sharks, and he has brought so much to our squad off and on the field.”
